en.title: Minimum Deletions to Form Count Groups
en.description:
The first number of a group states exactly how many group elements follow it. A sequence is valid if it can be split contiguously into several such groups; the empty sequence is also valid. Each operation deletes any one element. Find the minimum number of deletions.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers; 1≤n≤200000, 1≤a[i]≤100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: it can be split into [3,7,2,6] and [2,4,4], so no deletion is needed. Example 2: deleting the leading 3 leaves [2,1], which is still too short; deleting 3 and 2 leaves [1], which is also too short, so the best is to delete all 3. Example 3: split into [1,8] and [4,5,2,6,1], so the answer is 0.
hints: Do DP from back to front. The current position can be deleted at cost 1+dp[i+1]; or it can be used as a group head that keeps the next a[i] elements, at cost dp[i+a[i]+1], which requires staying in bounds.
